blocks.text:
# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container

self.assertEqual(_resolve_run_block(), _bench_yml_resolve_block())

    def test_default_provider_is_byte_identical_to_pre_gh1503_wiring(self):
        for provider in ("", "zai-glm-5.3-flash"):
            proc = _run_resolve(provider=provider)
            self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)
            outputs = _resolve_outputs(proc)
            self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_type"], "zai")
            self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_config"], self.LEGACY_ZAI_CONFIG)
            self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_key_env"], "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI")
            self.assertEqual(outputs["bench_model"], "glm-5.3-flash")
            self.assertEqual(outputs["run_label"], "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)")

    def test_kimi_for_coding_resolves_the_full_triple(self):
        proc = _run_resolve(provider="kimi-for-coding")
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)
        outputs = _resolve_outputs(proc)
        self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_type"], "kimi")
        self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_key_env"], "FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH")
        self.assertEqual(outputs["bench_model"], "k3-256k")
        self.assertEqual(outputs["run_label"], "kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)")
        config = json.loads(outputs["provider_config"])
        self.assertEqual(config["baseUrl"], "https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1")
        self.assertEqual(config["model"], "k3-256k")
        self.assertEqual(config["apiKeyEnvVar"], "FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH")
        # gh-1471 D4: the capability fields ride the config explicitly.
        self.assertEqual(config["contextWindow"], 200000)
        self.assertEqual(config["maxTokens"], 16384)

    def test_unknown_provider_fails_hard_with_no_outputs(self):
        proc = _run_resolve(provider="gpt-5")
        self.assertNotEqual(proc.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("unknown provider", proc.stdout + proc.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(_resolve_outputs(proc), {})

    def test_missing_kimi_secret_fails_naming_the_secret(self):
        proc = _run_resolve(provider="kimi-for-coding", kimi_key="")
        self.assertNotEqual(proc.returncode, 0)
        message = proc.stdout + proc.stderr
        self.assertIn("FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY", message)
        self.assertIn("kimi-for-coding", message)
        self.assertEqual(_resolve_outputs(proc), {})

run identity (run-name / job name / summary) carries provider+model,

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container

self.assertEqual(_resolve_run_block(), _bench_yml_resolve_block())

"""Pins the Bench Harbor dispatch defaults (issue #1316).

AC-first: these fail on the pre-#1316 workflow (4.0 dataset / modal env /
self-hosted runner) and pass after the migration flips the defaults to
Terminal-Bench 2.1 on the default Harbor `docker` sandbox, on ubuntu-latest.
Also pins the legacy `bench.yml` 0.1.1 default (issue #1316 req 6: the tb
1.x path stays untouched) and the adapter wiring the docker default rides
on (env type reaches `harbor run -e`; the #1122 timeout knob contract).

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa

gh-1503: the provider-selection port of bench.yml's gh-1471 design —
the setup-job resolve step is a BYTE-CONSISTENT copy of bench.yml's
(mirrored suite below executes the block extracted from
bench-harbor.yml), the shard env consumes the resolved triple, the
run identity (run-name / job name / summary) carries provider+model,
and the free-text `model` input is replaced by the resolved
bench_model output (REG-1: the default still resolves the exact
3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-gh-1503).

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value


@unittest.skipUnless(

)
class BenchHarborDefaultsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.text = _HARBOR_YML.read_text()

    def test_default_dataset_is_terminal_bench_2_1(self):
        # Issue #1316 req 4: default dataset is the 2.1 family; 2.0 (and
        # every other family) stays reachable via the same input.
        self.assertEqual(
            _workflow_input(self.text, "dataset"), FAMILIES["2.1"]
        )

    def test_default_cpu_env_is_docker(self):
        # Issue #1316 req 1: local docker is the default sandbox — no
        # Modal/cloud dependency for the default dispatch.
        self.assertEqual(_workflow_input(self.text, "cpu-env"), "docker")

    def test_default_cpu_runner_is_ubuntu_latest(self):
        # Issue #1316 req 1: GH runners already have docker.
        self.assertEqual(_workflow_input(self.text, "cpu-runner"), "ubuntu-latest")

    def test_adapter_and_timeout_wiring_intact(self):
        # The docker default must actually reach the harbor invocation and
        # the #1122 env contract must stay wired (issue #1316 reqs 2+5).
        self.assertIn('-e "$ENV_TYPE"', self.text)
        self.assertIn("export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC", self.text)
        # gh-1503: the zai hardcode is gone — the provider triple arrives
        # from the setup resolve step (same wiring as bench.yml gh-1471).
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}",
            self.text,
        )
        self.assertNotIn("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai", self.text)

    def test_n_concurrent_default_stays_one_with_kimi_documented(self):
        # gh-1503 req 6: 1 stays the default (z.ai rate-limit safe); the
        # kimi-safe guidance lives in the input description so the owner
        # picks the level at dispatch time.
        self.assertEqual(_workflow_input(self.text, "n-concurrent"), "1")
        description = self.text.split("n-concurrent:", 1)[1].split("\n", 2)[1]
        self.assertIn("kimi", description)

# wiring), kimi-for-coding k3-256k (FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom`

      - name: Resolve provider

            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)

              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.

              # flag the field first with a less precise message).

                [.. | objects | keys[]

import json

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding k3-256k (FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for k3-256k (shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding k3-256k (FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for k3-256k (shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

blocks.text:
# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (model id `kimi-for-coding` —
  the plan's own model name, needs the `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or
  `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.

      - name: Resolve provider

            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)

              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.

              # flag the field first with a less precise message).

                [.. | objects | keys[]

import json

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding k3-256k (FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for k3-256k (shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi

              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the Bench Harbor dispatch defaults (issue #1316).

AC-first: these fail on the pre-#1316 workflow (4.0 dataset / modal env /
self-hosted runner) and pass after the migration flips the defaults to
Terminal-Bench 2.1 on the default Harbor `docker` sandbox, on ubuntu-latest.
Also pins the legacy `bench.yml` 0.1.1 default (issue #1316 req 6: the tb
1.x path stays untouched) and the adapter wiring the docker default rides
on (env type reaches `harbor run -e`; the #1122 timeout knob contract).

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa

gh-1503: the provider-selection port of bench.yml's gh-1471 design —
the setup-job resolve step is a BYTE-CONSISTENT copy of bench.yml's
(mirrored suite below executes the block extracted from
bench-harbor.yml), the shard env consumes the resolved triple, the
run identity (run-name / job name / summary) carries provider+model,
and the free-text `model` input is replaced by the resolved
bench_model output (REG-1: the default still resolves the exact
3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-gh-1503).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from families import FAMILIES

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
_HARBOR_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench-harbor.yml"
_BENCH_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench.yml"


def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value


@unittest.skipUnless(
    _HARBOR_YML.exists(), "bench-harbor.yml not found (standalone bench checkout)"
)
class BenchHarborDefaultsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.text = _HARBOR_YML.read_text()

    def test_default_dataset_is_terminal_bench_2_1(self):
        # Issue #1316 req 4: default dataset is the 2.1 family; 2.0 (and
        # every other family) stays reachable via the same input.
        self.assertEqual(
            _workflow_input(self.text, "dataset"), FAMILIES["2.1"]

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

        # Issue #1316 req 4: default dataset is the 2.1 family; 2.0 (and

        self.assertEqual(

        # Issue #1316 req 1: local docker is the default sandbox — no
        # Modal/cloud dependency for the default dispatch.
        self.assertEqual(_workflow_input(self.text, "cpu-env"), "docker")

    def test_default_cpu_runner_is_ubuntu_latest(self):
        # Issue #1316 req 1: GH runners already have docker.
        self.assertEqual(_workflow_input(self.text, "cpu-runner"), "ubuntu-latest")

    def test_adapter_and_timeout_wiring_intact(self):
        # The docker default must actually reach the harbor invocation and

        self.assertIn('-e "$ENV_TYPE"', self.text)

        )

    def test_n_concurrent_default_stays_one_with_kimi_documented(self):
        # gh-1503 req 6: 1 stays the default (z.ai rate-limit safe); the

  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the

blocks.text:
# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1

              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,

              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the Bench Harbor dispatch defaults (issue #1316).

AC-first: these fail on the pre-#1316 workflow (4.0 dataset / modal env /
self-hosted runner) and pass after the migration flips the defaults to
Terminal-Bench 2.1 on the default Harbor `docker` sandbox, on ubuntu-latest.
Also pins the legacy `bench.yml` 0.1.1 default (issue #1316 req 6: the tb
1.x path stays untouched) and the adapter wiring the docker default rides
on (env type reaches `harbor run -e`; the #1122 timeout knob contract).

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa

gh-1503: the provider-selection port of bench.yml's gh-1471 design —
the setup-job resolve step is a BYTE-CONSISTENT copy of bench.yml's
(mirrored suite below executes the block extracted from
bench-harbor.yml), the shard env consumes the resolved triple, the
run identity (run-name / job name / summary) carries provider+model,
and the free-text `model` input is replaced by the resolved
bench_model output (REG-1: the default still resolves the exact
3-field zai JSON the workflow hardcoded pre-gh-1503).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from families import FAMILIES

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
_HARBOR_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench-harbor.yml"
_BENCH_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench.yml"


def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value


@unittest.skipUnless(
    _HARBOR_YML.exists(), "bench-harbor.yml not found (standalone bench checkout)"
)

        # Issue #1316 req 1: GH runners already have docker.
        self.assertEqual(_workflow_input(self.text, "cpu-runner"), "ubuntu-latest")

# base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container

self.assertEqual(_resolve_run_block(), _bench_yml_resolve_block())

            self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0, proc.stderr)

            self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_type"], "zai")
            self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_config"], self.LEGACY_ZAI_CONFIG)
            self.assertEqual(outputs["provider_key_env"], "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI")
            self.assertEqual(outputs["bench_model"], "glm-5.3-flash")
            self.assertEqual(outputs["run_label"], "zai-glm-5.3-flash (glm-5.3-flash)")

    def test_kimi_for_coding_resolves_the_full_triple(self):

        self.assertEqual(_resolve_outputs(proc), {})

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value
